messages:
Anika: Heads-up — onboarding 'aurora-lite-13b' (llama->gemma conversion) is showing a rotary-phase mismatch after GPTQ q4_0 quantization. Repro steps below, minimal repro attached.

Anika: Repro (quick):
```bash
# convert + quantize
python convert.py --src llama-ckpt --dst aurora-lite --out model.pt
python quantize.py --model model.pt --scheme q4_0 --out model.q4
# run small prompt
python serve.py --model model.q4 --prompt "The capital of France is" --max-tokens 8
```
Observed: tokens shift one position for several prompts, outputs like: 
`"The capital of France isParis"` (no space between token and punctuation), and attention weights in head 3 look scrambled.

Jon: Can you paste the raw logits diff vs FP16 baseline? quick check: `--dump-logits`

Anika: Pasted small snippet from dump (FP16 baseline -> q4):
```
logit_diff_mean: 0.0142
logit_diff_topk(1): 0.47
shifted_token_examples:
  baseline: ["Paris"]
  q4     : ["Paris", "</s>"] (duplicate eos)
```

Priya: :eyes: this smells like tokenizer/vocab aliasing + rotary index misalignment. Did the conversion step re-map special tokens?

Anika: I checked `tokenizer.vocab_size` and `tokenizer.get_vocab()`; sizes match but there are a few duplicate byte-sequence aliases in the new vocab. Example: `0xE2 0x80` sequence maps to two ids (rare). Might be normalization differences from the original tokenizer.

Sam: Also worth checking KV cache index offset — if the rotary angle uses a position index that was shifted by 1 during conversion we get headwise phase errors. Add a small probe: run the model with `--dump-kv idx=0..10` and compare k/v for first token between FP16 and q4.

Anika: I ran KV dump. Here's the short trace showing an off-by-one in `apply_rotary` call stack:
```
[apply_rotary] head=3 pos=0 angle_idx=1 expected=0.0 got=0.3927
[apply_rotary] head=3 pos=1 angle_idx=2 expected=0.3927 got=0.7854
# but baseline: pos=0 angle_idx=0
```

eval-bot: regression-suite/lexicon-smoke on model.q4 completed — fail: 12/432 tests (rotary-phase & tokenization). Full report: https://internal/reports/1759876543

ci-bot: quant-build #5242 finished for `aurora-lite-13b` (q4_0). artifact: s3://redwood-quant/aurora-lite/5242/model.q4

Jon: Quick hypothesis: the tokenizer conversion added a leading sentinel token in some sequences during conversion, causing position ids to be off by one when feeding cached KV. If true, rotary angle will be incorrectly indexed by `pos`.

Priya: Another angle — some GEMMA variants use headwise rotary frequencies (freq per head) vs global freq. Our quantizer currently bakes a single `rotary_scale` tensor into the weights; if the original used `head_scale`, quant + convert may collapse dims. Check shape of `rotary_scale`: should be `(num_heads, head_dim)` not `(head_dim,)`.

Sam: Quick patch idea: fallback to recompute rotary angles at runtime from `inv_freq` if shape mismatch detected. Pseudo: 
```
if rotary_scale.ndim == 1:
  inv_freq = compute_inv_freq(head_dim, base)
  rotary_scale = inv_freq.reshape(1, head_dim) * ones(num_heads, 1)
```
Would increase CPU cost but useful for triage.

Anika: I tried that locally — recomputing inv_freq fixed the phase alignment for small prompts, outputs match FP16 within tolerance on the lexicon smoke.

Jon: Can you open a minimal PR with the runtime fallback + a regression test? Mark it WIP and tag me. If that fixes we can decide whether to upstream a converter change (preferred) or maintain fallback for converted artifacts.

Anika: Created PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/9623 (WIP) — includes `rotary_fallback` flag and a test `tests/rotary_mismatch.py`.

Priya: Good. Also add a tokenizer normalization check in the onboarding harness: `normalize_unicode=True` and a check for duplicate byte-sequence aliases. If duplicates, fail conversion and prompt to normalize.

Sam: For the quant side, try q3_k (smaller group) to see if granularity affects collapse of headwise params. Also run `--quant-checksums` to verify parameter layout after quantize step.

Anika: Running q3_k now on a small shard — will post numbers. If q3_k behaves, we might prefer it as temporary. :thumbsup:

Jon: Assigning follow-ups: Anika (PR + regen artifacts), Priya (tokenizer normalization check), Sam (quant sanity runs q3_k vs q4_0). I'll coordinate with oncall if any customer impact.

Anika: Thanks — grabbing it now. :coffee:
